en: A-Anyway, I'll meet you guys in there!

That friggin' idiot. Don't he know how
t'thank his aniki? How embarrassin'.
Let's just hope he makes it in time.
Fer sure. Y'wanna head there, too?

We don't take male customers here.
Stay out if you know what's good for you.

B-But I jus' wanna use the bathroom.
Gimme a break!
My name's Kiryu.

I'm looking for the owner, Kazuki, or the
manager, Yuya. Can you get one of them?
I'm an old friend.

Kazuki? Yuya?
Nobody by those names here.

Now move along, gramps. We can't have
old fucks like you loitering out here.
Aniki. What's goin' on?

I'm not sure. Maybe we should try
asking one of the hosts.
Um, is that you, Kiryu-san?

You can't tell?
I guess I look a little different.
What about now?
It's you! Yuya!

Yuya? Oh yeah, Aniki. That's the guy
who y'called the manager.
Yep. I used to run Stardust.

But as you can tell, I'm just
a normal businessman now.

Wait, so you quit your job at Stardust?
What are you doing here then?

Hm? Oh, right.
You still okay, Yuta?
Need... Bathroom... Now...!
What's wrong with people in Tokyo?

They really need to get so upset about
a guy askin' to use the bathroom?

Y'sure y'didn't shit yerself?
No hot smears runnin' down yer pants?

Yeah, yeah. Think whatever y'want
if it helps ya sleep tonight.

Yuya. These two are part of a Hiroshima
yakuza family. They're helping me out.

I see. But going back to Haruka-chan...
Does she really have a son now?
Yeah, she really does.
Apparently this guy is the father.

Rumor has it he's a host in Kamurocho now.
His name's Tatsukawa.

I was thinking you two over at Stardust
might know something. Recognize him?
Actually... I do.
You do!?

Before I left, he was working
for us at Stardust.

Wow! Yer incredible, Aniki!
Y'found him straight away!

That said, I'm not sure if he's
still working there, though.
Stardust has changed a lot lately.

Not only did I leave the place, but
Kazuki-san doesn't even own it anymore.

This Kazuki-san...
Is he another friend of yours, Kiryu-aniki?

Yeah, though we haven't seen
each other in forever.

Kazuki and Yuya were always incredibly
helpful to me whenever I was in Kamurocho.
So what happened with Stardust, Yuya?

I always thought that club would
be nothing without the two of you.

It's been rough lately,
for both host clubs and cabarets.

Practically the city's whole entertainment
industry is in a huge slump at the moment.

This war between the Tojo Clan and
the triads has only made things worse.

Kazuki-san and I tried month after month,
but we kept coming out in the red.

An opportunity came along at
the beginning of this year, though.

These Koreans came into town with
enough capital to make an impact.

They used it to scoop up almost all the
prime real estate throughout Kamurocho.
Stardust happened to be one of those spots.
So the Koreans bought the place out?

Yeah. I didn't know it then, but apparently
they were backed by... the Jingweon.
Say what? Who're the Jingweon?

A Korean mafia. We have a long history.
I'm sure they hate me to this day.

But they fell apart a ways back, and
nobody left should know me personally.

Kiryu-aniki... You've even fought
against Korean mafia? Amazing.

You're right to guess that the Jingweon is
made up mostly of young guys nowadays.

Take the guy who bought Stardust. I bet he's
an officer, but he's still in his twenties.

D'ya think Tatsukawa'd really be able t'keep
workin' as a host there after they came in?
He'd probably quit, yeah?

Even if he did, there should still be
some clues about him at the club.

The Jingweon Mafia might be there,
but it's worth trying to get in for that.
You never change, Kiryu-san.

At the moment, I'm managing a small company
I know from my time in the host business.

I've had to re-learn everything from the
ground up to adjust to regular work.

I should be glad I even managed to find
a job, though, especially at my age.

Anyway, it really was chance that we ran into
each other outside of Stardust, Kiryu-san.
And what's Kazuki up to?

Well, he's trying to raise funds so he
can buy Stardust back from the Koreans.

Though I doubt he'll want to pull the
trigger while this war's raging on.

And if Kazuki does regain ownership,
you think you'd go back to work for him?
Of course. That should be obvious!

I'm the only one who's fit to be
Kazuki-san's right-hand man!

Interesting. Sounds like what you said
to me earlier applies to you as well.
And what was that?
You never change.
Hey, Kiryu-aniki...
Does this shop seem weird t'you?

Wh-What the!? Why ain't there
a single soul in the whole place!?

A few days ago, I heard you had returned to
Kamurocho. It's a great honor to meet you.

I hope you have time to drop by Stardust
after this. I'd love to show you the club.

You're pretty insistent on that.
Have we met somewhere before?

I'm simply an ardent fan of yours.
Is that a problem?

I'm actually glad to hear it.
I have some questions for you.

Y-Yeah, he's right! Is there a guy named
Tatsukawa workin' over at yer club?
We got a bone t'pick with him!
I'll answer your questions later.

First, you'll have to accept the invitation
I've extended to you. Is that all right?

Yeah, we'll be there soon.
Wait for us over at Stardust.

Perfect. In that case,
I'll see you shortly.

Kiryu-san, that guy is part of the Jingweon.
He's the one who bought Stardust from us.
You seriously want to meet with him?

As we speak, the Jingweon Mafia is trying
to butt into the conflict over Kamurocho.

Some rumors say they're even escalating
things between the Tojo Clan and the triads.

This isn't like before.
They're stronger now.

I understand the danger. But we have to
find Haruto's father, no matter the cost.

Figures. There's no point arguing.
You really are the same as always.

I'm glad we got to see each other again.
Take care, Yuya.
Of course. Same to you, Kiryu-san.

(I never thought I'd see the Jingweon again.
Let's see what's waiting for me at Stardust...)

[That's him! That's Kiryu!
Who are those two with him, though?]

[I don't care who they are.
Let's just kill them!]
A-Aniki. Those guys want somethin' from us.

They're yelling something in Korean...
Do y'think they could be...
The Jingweon Mafia.

Whaddya mean? Y'sayin' that Joon-gi Han
guy was jus' playin' at bein' nice?

I guess they're not all on the same page.
Some of them clearly still despise me.
[Die, Kiryu!]

We don't have time for this.
Come on.
[There he is! That's Kiryu!]
[Outta my way!]

We'll have to complain to
Joon-gi Han after this.

Man, Kamurocho sure is
a crazy place to be, Aniki.
Everyone's spoilin' fer a fight!
Cap. I think you jinxed us.

I'm sure Joon-gi Han is
getting tired of waiting.
Kiryu-aniki. We can handle these goons.
Y'oughta get on over t'Stardust.

We're gonna have some fun
without ya, though!

Listen to Cap, Kiryu-aniki.
We'll catch up with you later.
And you're sure you'll be okay?
We gotta focus on finding Tatsukawa.

If we can't help you with stuff like this,
what was the point of comin' to Tokyo?
Y'ready, Aniki? Get movin'!
Okay. Try to get there soon.
Yup!

I'm heatin' up now! Kinda hopin' these
bitches call up some more friends!
'Cause this ain't over by a long shot!

(I'm sure those two can handle this.
I need to hurry to Stardust.)
Cap said I should go n' catch up to you.

I'm so honored that you decided
to drop in, Kiryu-san.

No need to be so guarded.
Please, right this way.
What's going on with Nagumo?

He's totally fine. I think he was glad
for the chance to bash some heads.

Probably the perfect way to
get over Kiyomi-san, really.
I'm sure.

I have to say, I was worried by how long
it took you to get here, Kiryu-san!

You can blame that on your subordinates.
They clearly don't know how to treat a guest.

My men were giving you trouble?
My deepest apologies.

I expected them to have the common
sense not to do something so foolish.
I'll make sure they answer for it later.

That aside, isn't this place fabulous?
The previous owner had great taste.

Kind of sad then, how it started to stagnate.
It was in desperate need of a facelift.

Considering how empty it is,
I wouldn't say it really worked.

What a cruel thing to say.
But all you've seen is the front.
It makes for a convenient facade.

What truly entices our female patrons is
the intangible danger lurking in the back.

Furthermore, we believe this establishment will
assist us in regaining a foothold in Kamurocho.
"We"?
Haven't you realized who I am by now?
One of the Jingweon Mafia, right?

Indeed. I must admit, some within our
organization still hold grudges against you.

They claim you were responsible for driving
the Jingweon to the brink of destruction.
But that's just backward thinking.

Those who believe such nonsense are akin to a
poison inhibiting our impending resurrection.

To me, you don't differ much from the warlords
of old who invaded Korea so many years ago.

It is no longer practical to view
the Dragon of Dojima as our enemy.

At least for my part, I accept our
shared past as water under the bridge.
In that case, what do you want with me?

I'd like to get closer to you. I must convince
my subordinates to stop being so stubborn.
Meaning what exactly?

Before I tell you that, I would like to show
you behind the curtain of my little club here.
We can speak further afterward.
Follow me, if you would.
Kiryu-aniki. Are y'sure this is okay?

If he really wanted to kill me,
he would have already tried.
Is that how this works?

And assuming Tatsukawa is actually here,
he'd be in the back room, right?

This is no excuse for the depravity of this
place, but I actually prefer the upper floor.

However, our loyal customers much prefer
what we've created down here.

You would be shocked how many women
desire the direct stimulation of a man.
Certainly more than I'd expected.

When I first came to Kamurocho, it seemed
this country was bent on suppressing desire.

Take host clubs and cabaret clubs for example.
The two main sources of adult entertainment.

As you know, those industries thrive on
creating an appetite that goes unfulfilled.

The men who frequent cabaret clubs don't just
want to drink with the girls. They need more.

However, there is an impenetrable barrier
forever blocking them from that desire.

Host clubs are no different. Women are
drawn in to them by the flesh of youth.

So, I've stripped these people of the dignity
Japan adores, and in so doing set them free.
This is a revolutionary service.

You've made your point.
Unfortunately, I'm not interested.

But you can't leave quite yet,
now can you?

Are you not looking for
a certain Tatsukawa fellow?

That's right. He's here, isn't he?
Where can I find him?

It pains me to say, your Tatsukawa is
no longer working in our establishment.

Even so, I can offer you a little hint
as to where he might be.
It's the ring!

But before I can tell you what I know, I'd
like you to participate in a game of mine.
So your information comes at a price.
I'm glad you're so quick to understand.
Aniki. What exactly's goin' on here?

That ring is a stage of sorts in which
we pit our hosts against each other.

Under normal circumstances, our patrons
select which hosts they want to see fight.

For some reason, when the ladies here see
their precious hosts dripping with blood...
...They in turn drip with desire.
What're you talkin' about!?

But our main event today will be a test of
skill between myself and the Dragon of Dojima.

You needn't worry; this match will be
strictly one-on-one. So, do you accept?

That doesn't even deserve an answer. I'm not
going to be a showpiece for your patrons.

Let's go, Yuta. I'm not about to get in
a ring built by my enemies.

Hold on. If you lose in that ring, you'll
tell us what you know about Tatsukawa, right?
Precisely. That's a promise.
All right. Lemme have a go at you, then.
Yuta. What're you doing?

Aniki. I don't have any reason
t'say no to this fight.

Once I knock the stupid grin off his face,
we'll get all the information we need.

The only reason I'm in Kamurocho is so
I can find Tatsukawa and kick his ass.

After what he did to our Haruka-chan,
he's in for a world of hurt.

Just thinkin' about it makes my
blood start to boil.

So listen. I'll put on whatever show I need to
if it means getting a lead on Tatsukawa.
You mean...
Very well then.

What a shame that I was unable to
lure the Dragon of Dojima into my ring.
